H&P – Super Detailed

Consult Summary:
Young woman with a several-hour history of left-sided throbbing headache preceded by visual aura, associated with photophobia and two episodes of vomiting; clinical impression is migraine with aura, brain tumor felt unlikely; symptomatic treatment and safety-net advice given.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe throbbing headache on left side since ~12:00 today.  
• Onset & course: Began suddenly (patient “don’t know, it just happened”); intensity worsens with head/neck movement or leaning forward; ongoing at time of consult (a few hours).  
• Aura: “Zig-zag” lines and blurred vision in both eyes a few minutes before pain onset.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia (wearing sunglasses), nausea, 2 episodes of vomiting. No fever, no rash.  
• Previous similar episode: One similar headache a few weeks ago, lasted “couple of days,” improved with rest and unspecified painkillers. Not usually headache-prone.  
• Red-flag review: No speech disturbance, limb weakness/numbness, balance problems, breathlessness, or recent head injury.  
• Exacerbating factors: Movement of head/neck, leaning forward.  
• Relieving factors: Previously rest and OTC painkillers; none yet tried today.  
• Systems review: Otherwise negative per transcript.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  

Past Surgical History: not mentioned.  

Medications:
• Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive), dose/route/frequency not documented, taken for contraception for 3 months.  
• Occasional OTC painkillers in past (names/doses not specified).  

Allergies:
• Not discussed. (missing)

Social History:
• Lives alone.  
• Occupation: Fashion industry; reports high work-related stress.  
• Exercise: None.  
• Smoking: Denies.  
• Alcohol: Denies.  
• Recreational drugs: Not asked/undocumented.

Family History:
• Mother: Migraines, underactive thyroid.  
• No known family history of brain cancer or other neurologic disease.

Physical Examination:
No physical exam findings documented in transcript.

Investigations:
None performed or ordered during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Likely migraine with aura  
  • Assessment: Unilateral throbbing headache, visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, previous similar episode; no focal deficits or red-flag features to suggest intracranial mass or meningitis.  
  • Plan:  
    – Symptomatic therapy: Paracetamol; or combination analgesia such as Co-codamol; consider NSAID (Ibuprofen or Naproxen). (All doses/route/frequency not documented.)  
    – Advise rest in dark, quiet environment; adequate hydration.  
    – Initiate headache diary to identify triggers and frequency.  
    – Follow-up next week: reassess frequency; consider prophylactic migraine medication if attacks persist or increase.  
    – Safety-net: Return immediately if headache worsens, fails to improve within 2–3 days, develops weakness, visual loss, escalating neck pain, or other neurological changes.

Issue 2 – Contraceptive pill (Microgynon) and migraine  
  • Assessment: New-onset migraine since starting combined OCP 3 months ago (temporal association).  
  • Plan: Discuss at next review the potential role of estrogen-containing OCP in migraine with aura and consider alternative contraception if headaches persist or worsen.

General plan items  
  • Stress management: Encourage regular exercise and stress-relieving activities; discuss further at follow-up.  
  • Provide patient information leaflet on migraine and red-flag symptoms.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: Allergies, full medication list with doses, vitals, detailed neurological & general physical exam findings.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear conversation; occasional minor garble (“Lyme’s”) but clinical content understandable.
